title: Product Purgatory: why customers love it but don't buy, and how to find urgency
summary: Jason Cohen explains why a product can pass the polite-interest test and still not sell. First, apply the Magic Wand Test: would they take it free, fully implemented? Then find the missing ingredient, urgency, by narrowing your target to customers who need it right now.

principles.text: Run the Magic Wand Test: if it were free and fully implemented, would they say yes? Many say no.
principles.quote: So! Do you want me to wave this magic wand? Shockingly, the answer is often: "No."

principles.text: Customers see the friction, risk, time and cost of adopting; value must far exceed that activation energy.
principles.quote: Furthermore, it's not good enough for value to merely exceed penalty; the value must be far larger than the penalty.

principles.text: New companies carry extra risk with no brand or track record, so even free can be refused.
principles.quote: This challenge looms even larger for new companies, because you have neither brand nor track record.

principles.text: If the product passes the wand test but isn't bought, the missing ingredient is urgency: you aren't a top-three priority.
principles.quote: the problem exists, the customer knows it, the customer has budget, the customer has the desire... but there's no urgency, no reason it has to be done now.

principles.text: Escape Purgatory by narrowing your ICP to 'and needs it right now', then aim marketing, sales and features at that segment.
principles.quote: In general, you solve Purgatory by further narrowing your target market with a condition of "...and needs it right now."

principles.text: No product is always a top priority; there are segments where it is and segments where it isn't, so find the former.
principles.quote: There's no such thing as a product that is always valuable or always risky or always a top priority.
